mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: Rising Fed Funds rate in late-cycle tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4%, or IC > 0.05 over the next 20 days.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 coinciding with a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests labor market strengthening, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥50,000 and UNRATE decreases in the same month
regime_hint: Labor market improving with falling unemployment
failure_condition: IC < 0.1 over 60 days or SPX 60-day returns are not significantly positive when trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (GDP demand) of 3% or more for three consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as investor confidence in economic expansion drives equity valuation upgrades.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥3% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive when demand momentum persists but SPX underperforms.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% in the prior month triggers a negative S&P 500 5-day forward return as weak manufacturing signals near-term risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in the previous month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when INDPRO contraction occurs, or IC > 0.2.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 3% for two consecutive months in a low-inflation regime, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive as lower policy rates encourage equity valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 305
failure_condition: 20-day returns not significantly positive when trigger not met or CPIAUCSL > 305.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in UNRATE below 4% accompanied by a decline in HOUST (home sales) of 10% suggests labor market softening and reduced consumer confidence, leading to a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and HOUST decreases by ≥10% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day returns not negative when trigger occurs or IC > 0.15.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in RSAFS (retail sales) growth exceeding 8% over the prior month predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as strong retail demand supports optimism about economic recovery.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth rate increases by >8% month-over-month
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly positive when RSAFS acceleration is not observed.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining PAYEMS (job creation) below 100,000 with no recovery in HOUST (home sales) indicates labor market stagnation and weak consumer demand, resulting in a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 100,000 for two consecutive months and HOUST does not recover in either month
regime_hint: Stagnant labor and weak demand regime
failure_condition: 20-day returns not negative when trigger not met or IC > 0.1.
